claims.body: A raw net position is close to meaningless without its historical distribution. Managed money 'net long 141,648' says nothing; 'net long at the 76th percentile of five years' says it is elevated but not extreme.
claims.why_it_matters: Always read the percentile, not the headline number. Most retail commentary quotes the level.

claims.body: The cohorts sum to roughly zero by construction. Swap dealers at an extreme short are usually the other side of managed money at an extreme long — not an independent bearish vote.
claims.why_it_matters: Do not count both as separate evidence. Two cohorts at opposite extremes is one observation about crowding, not two.

claims.body: Positioning extremes describe the potential energy in a move, not its timing. Crowded positions can stay crowded for months and get more crowded first.
claims.why_it_matters: Use it to size down and to avoid chasing, not to fade. Fading an extreme without a price trigger is how you get run over.

claims.body: FX uses the TFF report (dealer, asset manager, leveraged funds); metals use the disaggregated report (producer/merchant, swap dealer, managed money). They are not interchangeable. Leveraged funds are the FX speculative cohort; managed money is the metals equivalent.
claims.why_it_matters: Comparing 'managed money' across gold and EURUSD is a category error — the field does not exist in the FX report.

claims.body: The CME contract is JPY/USD, so a long JPY futures position is SHORT USDJPY as conventionally quoted.
claims.why_it_matters: Get this wrong and every USDJPY positioning read is inverted. Argus flips the sign automatically; other sources often do not.
